Culture Spreading: New beats Old

Culture, communication and rumor spreading are part of human history, coupled to mere power struggles. This applet focus on the news and the fact that we are more interested in new news than in old news. This can be implemented in a model for culture spreading, using classical knowledge of word spreading in Japan. The model is here generalized to explore different parts of the world, and to consider that spreading across diluted area are slower than across more dense populated areas.

The model. Land is covered by a square lattice with spacing Δ. Every lattice site carries one word (say a swearword). New words are coined in one or more cultural centers. At each time step, every site on average once picks a random neighbour and passes its word on to it — but the word is only adopted if it is newer than the word already there (new > old). Old information is thus continually overrun by new information spreading out from the centers, which produces concentric, patchy word regions such as the aho/baka pattern around Kyoto.

Δ
lattice spacing (km). One time step corresponds to Δ years, since words spread ≈1 km/yr.
f
word frequency of a center: probability per time step that a new word is coined there.
p
probability that an old word resists a newer one (p = 0 is the pure new>old model).
Bridges
islands (separate lattice clusters) closer than a chosen distance are joined at their nearest points.
Sea routes
a two-point shortcut: the end points become direct neighbours.
Roads
a polyline along which a word spreads instantly to every site on the road.
Population model
optional variant where the site that communicates is chosen with probability proportional to the local population density (GPWv4, 2015) instead of uniformly; everything else is unchanged.

Reference. L. Lizana, N. Mitarai, K. Sneppen & H. Nakanishi, Modeling the spatial dynamics of culture spreading in the presence of cultural strongholds, Phys. Rev. E 83, 066116 (2011).
B. Dybiec, N. Mitarai & K. Sneppen, Information spreading and development of cultural centers, Phys. Rev. E 85, 056116 (2012).

Coastlines: Natural Earth. Population density: CIESIN Gridded Population of the World v4 (2015, 0.1°). Click Move on a center in the panel, then click the map, to relocate it.

Culture Spreading: New beats Old

New words are coined in cultural centers and copied to neighbouring lattice sites; a newer word always overrules an older one (unless p>0). All settings take effect immediately in the running simulation.

Map & lattice
1 time step = Δ years (spreading speed 1 km/yr). Spacings giving too many sites for this map are disabled.
Cultural centers
To move a center: press its Move button, then click the map.
